channel.title: BioFarmLab — Knowledge
channel.description: Knowledge about soil biology, compost and regenerative agriculture.

item.title: Chemical vs. biological soil testing: what does each one tell you?
item.description: Chemical testing measures pH and selected nutrients. Microscopy-based biological assessment shows the presence and proportions of major organism groups. The two methods answer different questions.

item.title: Can fertilizer replace soil biology?
item.description: Fertilizer can supply nutrients, but it does not replace decomposition, nutrient cycling, root–microbe interactions or the biological contribution to soil structure.

item.title: A compost turner: turning hours of work into minutes
item.description: Why use a compost turner? A machine that makes turning large windrows, composting horse manure and producing compost on the farm easier.

item.title: Soil or compost problem? Find the cause before you add another product
item.description: Field observation, chemistry, biological assessment and compost process signals provide different information. Start with the question you need answered.

item.title: Why is my compost pile not heating up?
item.description: A compost pile stays cool when microbial activity is limited or when the heat being produced escapes too quickly. The same symptom can have several causes.
